title: Shellbane Gryphon Guide (OSRS)
summary: A day-one guide to the Shellbane Gryphon, the new mid-level Slayer boss added with Sailing, which Gnomonkey calls possibly the easiest boss ever added, easier than Scurrius. He covers gear (including the weight-based knockback mechanic), the unlock requirements, the attack mechanics and the two unique drops, the Gryphon horn and the new rapier.

outline.text: Introduction: the new Slayer boss and basic Iron Man-style gear
Gear: Arkan blade, steel ring, Tortugan shield, black mask and the 45 kg weight mechanic
Inventory and preparation: fairy ring access and supplies
Requirements and location: Slayer unlock, 51 Slayer, 45 Sailing, Troubled Tortugans
Boss fight mechanics: tornadoes, acid corrosion, weight stun
Advanced tips: stacked tornado danger, weight demonstration, removing armour for corrosion
Rewards: Gryphon horn and the new rapier, and who should farm the boss

claims.text: Gnomonkey considers the Shellbane Gryphon, the new mid-level Slayer boss added with Sailing, maybe the easiest boss ever added to the game, easier than Scurrius.
The Shellbane Gryphon is weak to stab, so Gnomonkey brings an Arkan blade.
The Shellbane Gryphon requires 51 Slayer and 45 Sailing, and you must also complete the quest Troubled Tortugans, which unlocks at 45 Sailing.
To fight the Shellbane Gryphon you must unlock it as a Slayer task (Gnomonkey thinks it costs 80 Slayer points) and get it as a task; it can only be killed on task.
To reach the Shellbane Gryphon, use fairy ring CJQ, which takes you very close to the cave entrance just north of it; a Dramen staff is needed unless the diary is done.
The Shellbane Gryphon alternates between an occasional ranged attack and a melee attack, and performs a special attack every seven attacks.
Wearing the Tortugan shield means the Shellbane Gryphon's regular attacks do almost no damage, so trips can be tremendously longer.
Gnomonkey says there is very little going on with the Shellbane Gryphon: you basically just move occasionally and dodge everything while you attack.
Gnomonkey says as a main the Shellbane Gryphon drops are probably not worth it, but as an Iron Man there are some really good drops.
The Shellbane Gryphon has a mechanic where, if you have more than 45 kilograms of weight equipped, you block its knockback attack.
If you are under 45 kg equipped, the Shellbane Gryphon's knockback attack hits for roughly 10 to 30 damage and throws you backwards.
If you have over 45 kg equipped, the Shellbane Gryphon is stunned instead, you block the damage and you get a bonus hit (two swings) on the boss.
Only equipped weight counts for the Shellbane Gryphon mechanic, not the weight of your inventory; Gnomonkey demonstrated taking off his body armour and being knocked back, taking a 28.
Gnomonkey says to disassemble your Slayer helmet with the right-click disassemble option and wear a black mask instead for the Shellbane Gryphon, because the black mask is heavier.

Gnomonkey notes a steel ring (a drop from the Deranged archaeologist on Fossil Island) is really heavy and useful for reaching the weight threshold, and mixed hide boots are a little heavier than climbing boots.
If you cannot get over 45 kg equipped you can still easily kill the Shellbane Gryphon; you just take a little extra damage.

As one of its specials, the Shellbane Gryphon places tornadoes on the ground near your feet roughly every five ticks (Gnomonkey is unsure of the exact timing); they grow into larger tornadoes, hurt you every tick if you stand on them, and explode if you are next to them.
The Shellbane Gryphon's acid attack is easy to dodge by stepping out of the way; if it hits you it applies a status effect called corrosion that hits you for 3s with a new hit splat.

To stop the corrosion damage from the Shellbane Gryphon's acid, take off all armour that gives defensive bonuses (including the ring); Gnomonkey notes this is awkward because you may have to drop items to make inventory space.

If you ignore the Shellbane Gryphon's tornadoes and five stack on top of you, they explode for about 70 damage (Gnomonkey saw hits of 60 and 70); this is the only thing that can really hurt or kill you in the fight.
Gnomonkey says the stacked tornadoes only hurt you if you fall asleep; moving a little bit avoids them entirely.

Gnomonkey approaches the Shellbane Gryphon from the perspective of an Iron Man starting bossing, using an Arkan blade, Barrows gloves, mixed hide boots, a steel ring, and tank armour from Barrows (or Rune platebody and legs are fine).
Gnomonkey considers the Arkan blade, a spec weapon from the quest that unlocks Mocha, a decent stab weapon and decent spec that works okay at the Shellbane Gryphon.
A Berserker ring is really good for the Shellbane Gryphon, but running no ring is also fine.

The Tortugan shield, a quest item from the quest that unlocks the Shellbane Gryphon, blocks almost all of the damage the Gryphon does; Gnomonkey says without it melee hits are basically guaranteed and with it they do not hit at all.
For supplies Gnomonkey brings supers, some prayer potions, and food, saying lower tier food is fine, plus a teleport away.
The Shellbane Gryphon drops feathers that charge its horn; the horn gives a passive Hunter boost and a 10% chance to double Hunter catches.
Gnomonkey says the horn is very solid for hunting chinchompas and similar creatures, such as cotton-type catches.
Gnomonkey describes the new rapier, Belle's folly, as a very slow, heavy-hitting stab weapon, basically the Zombie axe but for stab.
Gnomonkey considers the rapier an excellent option for Tombs of Amascut and very good for killing Eclipse Moon, a really good mid-level stab weapon.
Gnomonkey suggests Irons planning to do Moons and then Tombs of Amascut can use the rapier to skip getting a Hasta; he says it is almost as good as a Hasta in Tombs of Amascut and very accurate.

Gnomonkey says the Black Kirus (as transcribed) exists and is better than the rapier but takes a while to obtain, so get the rapier first and swap to the Black Kirus later, or to a Fang if you get one.
Sailing launched with a new mid-level Slayer boss, the Shellbane Gryphon, and this guide was made on release day.
Gnomonkey describes this as a Day 1 guide in which some things may change and a better meta may appear in a few weeks.
